summary: The 'prepared_gaia' project is a robust and well-designed multi-agent system that faithfully implements the GAIA methodology. It addresses all project requirements using safe communication patterns and correct asynchronous execution logic.

findings.description: The system explicitly maps to GAIA roles (WK, PK, IS, WE, SIM, GUI), providing a clear and professional multi-agent structure.
findings.evidence: Docstrings and class names like DetectionAgent (WK) and PredictionAgent (PK) in src/main.py

findings.description: Communication is implemented via a custom MessageBroker using asyncio.Queue, allowing for asynchronous, decoupled agent interaction without external dependencies.
findings.evidence: class MessageBroker and asyncio.create_task(agent.run()) in src/main.py

findings.description: The system uses JSON for message serialization, which is a safe and standard practice.
findings.evidence: json.dumps() and json.loads() (implicitly via manual parsing) in src/main.py

findings.description: All stakeholder notifications (admin, students, disinfection) are represented in the agent roles and message types.
findings.evidence: ROACH_DETECTION_MSG, DISINFECTION_MSG, and NotificationAgent in src/main.py

findings.description: The system lacks a formal type validation library like Pydantic, relying on manual dictionary conversions which can be error-prone as the system scales.
findings.evidence: Manual to_dict() and from_dict() methods in message classes.
